A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same semantic-conditional graph reasoning framework, renamed from SCORE to SCR. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support a reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original KG reasoning, node classification and graph classification experiments, together with component ablations and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds broader KG evaluation, restricted-label experiments, additional ablations and an empirical parameter analysis.

M1.justification: The feature unifier, augmented relation graph, semantic initialization, two-channel fusion and training loss remain recognizable across versions. However, v1 describes shared trainable parameters in both channels, while v2 Section 4.2 calls the semantic channel frozen/non-parametric while retaining parameter sharing. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes optimization or clarifies existing implementation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates 24 inductive KG datasets, six node classification datasets and eight graph classification datasets. v2 retains this coverage and adds substantial inductive and transductive KG evaluation, including WikiTopics, ILPC2022, Hetionet, ConceptNet100k and YAGO310. Appendix K reports coverage of 54 evaluation graphs plus the three pretraining graphs.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds a fully trained GIN comparator for graph classification. Table 10 also adds node accuracy comparisons with one-shot GCN and pretraining/fine-tuning. The principal KG and graph foundation model comparators remain; the graph prompt baselines are retained in appendix comparisons rather than removed entirely.

E3.justification: v2 introduces restricted-label evaluations using 20% of training label edges or five edges per class, and separate node comparisons with 90% of samples reserved for testing. It also reports a four-KG SCR training configuration and average-rank metrics. These extend the evaluation design; newly disclosed settings for retained results do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 3 extends component ablations to node and graph classification and adds removal of relation-specific embeddings through 'w/o RelDiff'. Section 5.5 tests dependence on available label edges, and Appendix H empirically checks initialization assumptions. The original hyperparameter heatmaps are retained and merged, while the original KG Hits@10 ablation panel is absent.

E5.justification: Both versions report classification results with plus/minus values and KG results as point estimates. Neither supplies explicit repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures. Additional result rows retain the existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 results remain unchanged, but v2 adds expanded KG results, restricted-label and 90%-test results, GIN comparisons, additional ablations and SCR(4g) scores. Existing baseline values also change: ULTRA's COLLAB and DD accuracies fall from 64.53 and 70.38 in v1 Table 11 to 51.80 and 43.52 in v2 Table 3. New split/budget results are separate evaluations, not same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: v1's Theorem 1 and Appendix D analyze SCMP versus CMP through relational Weisfeiler-Leman reasoning and a layer-equivalence proposition. v2 replaces this with Appendix F's architectural reduction to ULTRA and a claimed strict expressivity advantage from semantic information. Section 4.1 and Appendix E also introduce formal task-graph definitions and label-to-link correspondence arguments.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a KG-trained semantic reasoning framework that transfers without task-specific fine-tuning to KG reasoning, node classification and graph classification. Both versions retain the 38-dataset headline and claims of gains over foundation models and supervised baselines. The new title and emphasis on pretraining sharpen this existing contribution rather than change its core scope.

C2.justification: v2 explains GraphAny's heterophilic advantage through label-based analytical tuning, replacing v1's emphasis on a mismatch between KG neighborhood learning and heterophily. It adds an argument that structural conditioning mitigates memorization of overlapping triples and specifies practical limitations at millions or billions of triples. The original limitations concerning training diversity and scalability remain.

D1.justification: v2 discloses concrete semantic-neighbor settings: delta=0.9, k=2 for node tasks, and k=1 or 3 for graph tasks. It specifies torch.svd_lowrank with q=d and niter=2 and expands task-conversion and label-access instructions. Hardware and the ULTRA code basis remain unchanged. Conversely, v1's per-dataset supervised-SOTA identifiers disappear from the dataset statistics table.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for OFA, ZeroG, KG-ICL, TRIX, SGC and newer transferability research, while removing some earlier application and expressivity references. Most existing related-work coverage remains. The new main-text section makes the contrast between KG-only pretraining and other graph transfer approaches more explicit.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, SCORE becomes SCR, and the narrative shifts from three semantic-isolation categories to task-format and semantic-transfer challenges. Related work gains a main-text section, methodology is reordered around task conversion, and substantial implementation, theory and sensitivity material moves to reorganized appendices. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column ACM layout with a single-column format and substantially redraws the framework diagram. Main classification tables now display the full dataset coverage previously partly relegated to appendices, with learning-paradigm and average-rank columns. The ablation figure is redesigned, the two sensitivity figures are merged, and new KG and restricted-label tables are added.

improvement.justification: Broader KG evaluation, label-availability controls, additional ablations and clearer settings make v2's transfer claims easier to assess than v1's. The revised organization also improves accessibility. These gains are tempered by unexplained baseline-score revisions and a weakness in the replacement expressivity argument: Appendix F invokes Lipschitz continuity to preserve positive separation after fusion, which that property alone does not establish.
